article_title: PostgreSQL 19's Delay, curl's Open Reporting of Minor Flaws and Edge's Review Automation: Where Three Projects Say AI-Assisted Work Lands

content_preview.title: PostgreSQL 19's Delay, curl's Open Reporting of Minor Flaws and Edge's Review Automation: Where Three Projects Say AI-Assisted Work Lands
content_preview.summary: Project sources link PostgreSQL 19's delay, curl's move of low and medium reports to public issues and Edge's extension-review automation to AI-assisted work; sources differ on how much of the PostgreSQL delay LLMs explain.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Background

Three pieces of project infrastructure that sit between a contribution and a release are the subject of this analysis: a database project's stabilisation period, a library's vulnerability-report intake and a browser vendor's extension review. Each has been described in October or September reporting as absorbing more work as AI tools enter the process.

The Herald has covered the individual developments. It reported on [PostgreSQL 19's release candidate and the November 19 general...

editor_notes.content_quality: A cross-project Analysis of 1,520 words (about 1,500 with link URLs stripped; range 800-2000). It compares PostgreSQL 19's delay, curl's move of LOW/MEDIUM vulnerability reports to public GitHub issues, Edge's extension-review automation, QEMU's report flood and Sashiko, and examines a disagreement between sources over cause. Reported facts and the Implications section are separated, the latter is framed as drawn from the sources, and the evidence-uneven paragraph is candid that three projects cannot establish a general pattern. It is a modest synthesis rather than a deep one, but it is a topic examination, not a recap of one release.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all 8 snapshots (source-0..7.html.gz), all HTTP 200 and non-empty, none with suspicious_patterns. (0) The Register, Lindsay Clark, Oct 16: confirms late Sept/early Oct slated, GA around Nov 19, 8-10 features dropped, Eisentraut 'veep at EDB' and leading committer, 'could be at least in part attributed to the LLM code reviews', the 'staring at a list of forty defect reports' / 'fixed overhead' / 'run out of time' quotes, 'vibe coding' remark, and the forward-looking remark verbatim: 'Unless the capabilities of LLM-assisted code review keep improving at the current rate, this situation should sort itself out for future development cycles'. The 'PARTNER CONTENT: Michael Stonebraker and Bruce Momjian' item is a separate sidebar teaser, not the cited article, and the cited article is not sponsored. (1) LWN, Joe Brockmeier, Sept 10: confirms Aug 25 'scary patch contest' email from Haas, Haas asked Claude to evaluate the scariest patches, April 8 feature freeze, Plageman and Bossart quotes verbatim, Gustafsson quote verbatim ('written, reviewed and tested, before AI tools were either available or even remotely as good as they are now'), Haas observation that features with many post-freeze fixes were committed close to freeze, Jungwirth/Misch 'with some LLM investigation'. Speakers all correctly attributed. (2) Phoronix, Michael Larabel, Oct 30: confirms Haas blog relay and both quoted factors verbatim; it adds nothing beyond the blog and is a relay (not original reporting). (3) daniel.haxx.se, Stenberg, Oct 20: first-party; confirms Oct 26 effective date, LOW/MEDIUM to GitHub, HIGH/CRITICAL on HackerOne, 'over 90%', 'entirely triggered by the current avalanche', 'brought to the brink of what we can muster', 'army of AI-using researchers', 'crazy sequences or option combinations', 'slightly longer window of opportunity'. (4) The Register, Simon Sharwood, Sept 9: confirms Edge quotes, 'strain', automation of repeatable checks, 'doesn't change our review standards', redundancies, and that the automation's use of AI is not disclosed. (5) Phoronix, Aug 25: Berrangé's Mastodon quote ('125 separate bug reports in under 10 minutes, all for ubsan reports', 'denial of service attack') verified; the quoted statement itself does not say the reports were AI-generated, only Larabel's framing does, exactly as the article states; rate-limit suggestion confirmed. (6) The Register, Richard Speed, Oct 21: confirms 52%, 25%, 31%, 21%, 35%, 32% and the Stenberg quote. (7) Phoronix Oct 8: Sashiko figures (191k reviews, 99 lists, 463 CVEs this year) confirmed; correctly labelled as the developers' own figures relayed by Phoronix. Allowlist: theregister.com, lwn.net, phoronix.com and daniel.haxx.se are all on config/source_allowlist.txt (exact hostname); no allowlist edits needed. INDEPENDENT-SOURCE COUNT: 3 independent outlets (The Register counted once across three articles; LWN, original reporting of the mailing list; Phoronix counted once, though its Haas and Sashiko items are relays of Haas's blog and a conference talk, and only the QEMU item relays a first-hand statement). Not independent: the curl blog (first-party). The Edge post and Linux Foundation survey are only reached through The Register. Even discounting Phoronix entirely, The Register and LWN make 2 independent outlets, and 8 sources total, so the Analysis requirements (>=4 sources, >=2 independent) are met.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All quotes and figures verified verbatim against snapshots and attributed to the right party. One framing issue, filed as a clarification: the Implications paragraph says 'on LWN, Haas questioned a simple LLM explanation and pointed to the timing of commits' as if it were a current disagreement about the PostgreSQL 19 delay. LWN's account is of a mailing-list exchange of August-September 2026 (published Sept 10), before the delay was announced; Haas's remark there was that he was not convinced 'the problem with Gustafsson's patch' (the online data-checksums patch) was as simple as finding more bugs with LLMs. Haas's Oct 30 blog (via Phoronix) later attributes the late release to LLM-found bugs. So the Haas positions differ by date and context rather than being contemporaneous. Gustafsson's and Eisentraut's statements are in practice close (both say the large features predate capable LLM review). The Phoronix line 'Haas's blog, per Phoronix, says the delay is AI's fault' tracks the blog's own title ('Postgres 19 is late, and it's AI's fault' per PR #2748 coverage). Title check: 'Where Three Projects Say AI-Assisted Work Lands' is the Herald's own synthesis; the body attributes each project's statements to named parties and notes the Edge automation's AI use is undisclosed and that three projects are too few for a general pattern. The title is slightly stronger than the sources (Edge says submission volume rose and review is strained; it does not itself say where AI work 'lands'), which I judged acceptable because the body flags it.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral. No loaded language, no AI self-reference, no predictions presented as the Herald's own (Eisentraut's expectation is explicitly his).
editor_notes.originality: Overlap with PR #2748 / 2026-10/31 'Robert Haas Attributes PostgreSQL 19's Late Release...' (News, merged): that piece covers Haas's blog as primary text with commit counts (>60% back-patched). This Analysis does not cite the blog and omits the counts, relying on Phoronix and LWN; no contradiction: both say Haas attributes the delay to LLM-found bugs, and the dates (April 8 freeze, reverts) are consistent (the Haas blog gives reverts Aug 27 - Sept 15). The Analysis adds the Eisentraut/Register account, LWN's mailing-list voices, curl, Edge, QEMU, Sashiko and the Linux Foundation survey, and compares them, so it is not duplicative. Internal links: all four (/article/2026-10/17-postgresql-19-rc-1..., /article/2026-09/10-microsoft-edge-team..., /article/2026-10/21-linux-foundation-research..., /article/2026-10/27-disclosure-rules-shift...) exist and are described accurately. No orphan URLs (body URLs equal article.sources).
concerns: The sentence 'None of the cited reports quantifies the share of delay attributable to LLM-found bugs' is true of the eight cited sources, but Haas's own blog (published, allowlisted since PR #2748, not cited here) gives commit counts including a back-patched-commit jump of more than 60%. Readers of the sibling article may read the sentence as stronger than it is; it is a statement about the cited sources only. Flagged, not corrected (the blog quantifies back-patching, not the share of the delay).
Haas LWN remark presented alongside his October blog without dating the shift; handled by the clarification correction.
Two of the three Phoronix items are relays of first-party material; the independent-outlet count rests chiefly on The Register and LWN.
recommendations: When a sibling article on the same story is in the same batch, cite or acknowledge it in the 'What we don't know' section.
Date contrasting positions held by the same person.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Meets the Analysis requirements (8 sources, 3 independent outlets, a real examination of a disagreement); all quotes verify. One clarification about the timing and scope of Haas's LWN remark is filed and the article publishes with it. Featured candidacy: 1 - accurate cross-project synthesis for a defined developer and maintainer audience; the underlying reports are secondhand and the pattern is acknowledged as thin
